AgentTurnCompletedPayload.description:
Persistent bridge event: full-turn aggregation (SDD §11.4).

Carries the complete aggregated thinking, the complete assistant message
text and the tool-call summary for one turn. Replay-safe: a freshly
opened or reconnected frontend renders the turn from this single event
instead of thousands of ephemeral stream-chunks.
AgentTurnCompletedPayload.title: AgentTurnCompletedPayload

AttemptHistoryPage.description: Full Attempt history for a Run (SDD §10.1 — GET /v1/runs/{id}/attempts).
AttemptHistoryPage.title: AttemptHistoryPage

ChatCommand.description:
Free-form conversation entry (Phase 3.6 frontend launcher).

The message is parsed into an IntentPlan (control/chat.py) and the Run is
created through the same CreateRunCommand semantics; follow-up questions
continue through the existing followup chain.
ChatCommand.title: ChatCommand

FinalCheckpointRequest.description:
Terminal checkpoint commit: runtime subject + lease facts + summary.

Extends ``RestoreRequest`` so the Pod can keep signing its CAS writes with
the fresh lease facts (owner/version) — the shared commit handler reads
them from the ``context`` bundle. ``agent_state`` carries the terminal
Agent snapshot (same ``pi-agent-core/v1`` schema as turn-level checkpoints)
— the final Checkpoint is what a follow-up / rerun Attempt restores from,
so dropping it would break history hydration across rounds.
FinalCheckpointRequest.title: FinalCheckpointRequest

FollowupHistoryPage.description: Paginated followup history for a Run.
FollowupHistoryPage.title: FollowupHistoryPage

FollowupRecord.description:
One question/answer (or in-flight question) stored for a Run.

``PENDING`` rows are durably queued for a fresh Attempt and have no answer
yet; ``ANSWERED`` rows carry the persisted answer (SDD §6.4).
FollowupRecord.title: FollowupRecord

HeartbeatResponse.description: Refreshed RuntimeContext (the new lease_version is a CAS prerequisite).
HeartbeatResponse.title: HeartbeatResponse

ModelCallRequest.description:
A full LLM call proxied from the Pod runtime (HttpStream).

Mirrors the PipeStream wire contract: complete message history + tool
definitions + sampling options; the Control Plane proxies to the real
provider through its RunSessionProvider and returns non-streaming content
blocks (text / tool_use / thinking).

``execution_unit_id`` is part of the bootstrap-granted subject the Pod
always signs with (see RestoreRequest).
ModelCallRequest.title: ModelCallRequest

ModelCallResponse.description:
Non-streaming LLM response (content blocks + stop_reason + usage).

The Pod's HttpStream translates this back into
``AsyncIterator[AssistantMessageEvent]`` for pi-agent-core (same shape the
pipe stream emits).
ModelCallResponse.title: ModelCallResponse

ReadToolResponse.description: Resource proxy result returned to the Pod's remote_read_tool.
ReadToolResponse.title: ReadToolResponse

RestoreResponse.description: Full checkpoint payload for the Pod runner to rehydrate its Agent.
RestoreResponse.title: RestoreResponse

ToolCallSummary.description: One aggregated tool call inside an ``agent.turn.completed`` payload.
ToolCallSummary.title: ToolCallSummary

ToolExecutionStartedPayload.description:
Persistent bridge event: pi-agent-core ToolExecutionStartEvent.

Durable (append_event -> PG -> Outbox -> SSE) so a reconnecting frontend
can render the tool activity from the event log alone. ``args`` is the
bounded, redacted-at-source argument snapshot; never raw credentials.
ToolExecutionStartedPayload.title: ToolExecutionStartedPayload

TurnCheckpointRequest.description:
Turn-level (mid-run) Checkpoint commit carrying the Agent snapshot.

Same runtime subject + lease facts as HeartbeatRequest, plus the
pi-agent-core Agent state snapshot persisted at TurnEnd (the safe
checkpoint boundary, SDD §5.5).
TurnCheckpointRequest.title: TurnCheckpointRequest

post.description:
Free-form conversation entry (Phase 3.6 frontend launcher).

Parses the natural-language message into an IntentPlan, then creates the
Run through the exact same CreateRunCommand semantics as POST /runs
(same idempotency, authorization and parameter-model guards). Follow-up
questions continue through the existing followup chain.

Return the follow-up history for a Run.
